meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Cook Islands (Realm of New Zealand; self-governing state in free association with New Zealand)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (English and New Zealand common-law heritage with local statutory overlay; the Cook Islands High Court and Court of Appeal apply Cook Islands statutes, New Zealand legislation pursuant to free-association constitutional arrangements, and relevant Commonwealth precedent)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: New Zealand – Hong Kong SAR Investment Agreement (2019)
New Zealand – China Agreement on the Promotion and Protection of Investments (ratified 2009, with 2019 Investment Protocol)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP, entered into force 2018 for New Zealand)
New Zealand – Australia Double Taxation Agreement (DTA, 2009)
New Zealand – United States Double Taxation Convention (1982, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Cook Islands: International Companies Act 2011 (No. 6 of 2011, as amended, repealing the International Companies Act 1981-82); Anti-Money Laundering and Countering of Terrorism Act 2004 (as amended); AML/CFT Code 2008; Financial Supervisory Commission Act 2003; and the 2018-19 beneficial-ownership amendments establishing a confidential central UBO register at the Financial Supervisory Commission. Realm of New Zealand: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (New Zealand), Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), and Sanctions Act 2019 (New Zealand) apply at the Realm level; the Cook Islands maintains its own separate registry and its own confidentiality and AML/CFT enforcement regime.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (confidential beneficial-ownership register maintained by the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission and the licensed registered agent; no public access to the shareholders, directors, or UBO file; nominee shareholders are permissible provided the underlying beneficial owner is fully disclosed to the registered agent and the Commission)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport (or national identity card) of each UBO, director, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of origin of the principal
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Consular Legalization; alternatively, Hague Apostille where both the issuing state and the receiving state are members of the 1961 Apostille Convention and the apostille is issued by the competent authority of the issuing state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (original or certified bank statement or utility bill dated within three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy with Consular Legalization or Hague Apostille as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming good standing and source of funds, or professional standing reference from a chartered accountant or commercial counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Reference bank or licensed professional adviser
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Consular Legalization or Hague Apostille as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Curriculum vitae and professional background statement of each proposed director and shareholder, including details of institutional or sovereign-wealth investors where applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicant principal (attested before a notary public)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized attestation followed by Consular Legalization or Hague Apostille as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Executed power of attorney and engagement letter appointing the Cook Islands licensed registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature verification with Consular Legalization or Hague Apostille as applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory layered screening of all UBOs, directors, authorized signatories, and beneficial-client counterparties against the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission sanctions notices, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC List of Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN/SSI list), the New Zealand Sanctions Act 2019 and associated targeted financial sanctions regulations, and the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; adverse-media and PEP-status verification is mandatory at onboarding, at each change of shareholder or signatory, and on a rolling six-month basis; any PEP association, sanctions-flag, or adverse-media finding automatically elevates the client risk rating to 'High Risk' and triggers enhanced due diligence, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) – International Companies Registry; filings are submitted electronically by the licensed registered agent via the FSC online document-filing system (no direct public filing access for non-licensed persons)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed in the Latin (Roman) alphabet; names may be in English or in a foreign language provided an approved English transliteration is included; the name must end with a limited-liability suffix or an approved abbreviation (such as 'Limited', 'Ltd.', 'Corporation', 'Corp.', 'Incorporated', 'Inc.', 'Pty Ltd.', 'S.A.', or 'N.V.'); the name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any name on the Cook Islands register, any defensive-name list, or, to the extent observable, the New Zealand Companies Register; no statutory license is required for ISIC 7310 public-relations activities, and no industry-specific consent token is therefore mandated for the ordinary PR agency name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of the proposed name, the licensed registered agent must file a written Request for Reconsideration with the Registrar of the International Companies Registry within 14 days, setting out (i) the grounds of distinctiveness and non-confusion, (ii) evidence of prior use, trademark registration, or client recognition of the mark, and (iii) the proposed alternative suffix or minor amendment if the objection concerns the limited-liability indicator; an adverse determination may be appealed to the Cook Islands High Court by way of judicial review within 30 days of notification; concurrently, the applicant may secure a fresh reservation under an alternative name without forfeiting the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible with statutory constraints: a licensed registered agent in the Cook Islands must maintain the statutory registered office, and the company's actual media and public-relations operations may be managed remotely through a virtual or back-office administration. ISIC 7310 international media relations and crisis PR services are not licensed activities, so no local trading premises, local staff, or physical operational substance are required; however, all statutory records, the register of members, the UBO file, and the company seal must remain at the registered office, and the registered agent must hold a complete client-due-diligence file at all times.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated at 5–15% for a standard low-risk International Company operating a non-licensed public-relations advisory business within the first three years of registration; inspection probability rises sharply to 50–75% where enhanced due diligence is triggered (PEP involvement, sanctions-flag, adverse media, or a suspicious-transaction report), in which case the Financial Supervisory Commission may require production of client files and source-of-funds evidence within 48 hours under the AML/CFT Code 2008.
